do_not_assume: A hidden control prevents unauthorized requests.
Authorization checked during initialization remains valid.
A previous C# block instance retains state.
A success response proves that all submitted values were persisted.
Stop when authorization succeeds through an intentional rule; do not bypass the server check or trust client visibility.
goal: A server action that accepts client data without trusting client state.
steps: Define a typed request and response contract.
Validate required values and identifier formats.
Load the authoritative entity in the action.
Evaluate the current person’s authorization for the exact operation.
Apply business rules and persist the change.
Return a structured result.
Invoke the action from TypeScript and handle both success and failure.
Verify the result through a fresh read when persistence is material. (Creating Blocks)
Confirm the server action checks the current person’s ordinary authorization.
If a child control needs delegated access, confirm the block created and provided a security grant.
Confirm the control injected the current token and included it in the request.
Confirm the endpoint reconstructs the grant and checks the authorization action needed for this operation.
Check whether the one-hour default token lifetime requires renewal.

goal: A standardized detail block with an explicit write boundary.
steps: Choose entity or CMS security.
If replacing an unsecured WebForms block, start with CMS security and review effective page permissions.
Generate the core detail block and related view models when the core generator is available.
Include properties needed for rendering or UI decisions.
Remove UI-only properties from the saveable-property list.
Confirm the entity metadata required by the detail component.
Build and run the boilerplate before adding custom logic.
Test view, edit, unauthorized access, validation failure, and save readback. (Creating Detail Blocks)

do_not_assume: Paging reduces data transfer.
A person link proves access to the destination.
A hidden column is excluded from export.
A visual delete confirmation replaces server authorization.
goal: A grid whose filters, exports, and actions operate on the intended rows.
steps: Bound the server query to an acceptable total result size.
Build the grid definition and row data.
Set a unique key field.
Choose typed columns for standard data and a generic `Column` only for custom markup.
Configure `hideOnScreen` and `excludeFromExport` independently.
Add filters, selection, edit, delete, security, copy, or reorder columns as needed.
For asynchronous handlers, return their Promises so controls remain disabled while work is pending.
Test row identity after sorting and filtering.
Test export behavior separately from on-screen visibility. (Grid, Standard Columns)
Measure or inspect the total row count, not only the configured page size.
Confirm whether the complete result set is being transferred to the browser.
Reduce or constrain the server result set if the business requirement permits.
Reassess attribute payloads and other per-row data.
Stop when the initial transfer and browser work are acceptable; changing only client page size does not reduce the payload. (Grids)

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A registered core field type with compatible server and client representations.
steps: Declare Obsidian platform support in the C# field type.
Expose its GUID through the field-type system GUID definitions and generation process.
Create the TypeScript field implementation and components.
Import and register the implementation in the field-type index.
Define safe public value and configuration representations.
Implement conversion back to the private stored representations where required.
Ensure formatting functions accept both display and unsaved edit representations.
Test equivalent attribute configuration and editing through WebForms and Obsidian blocks.
Add an example to the field-type gallery when following the documented core workflow. (Converting Core Field Types)
Compare the public display and public edit representations.
Pass representative values from both forms through `getTextValue` and related formatting methods.
Update those methods to handle either representation.
Confirm the conversion back to the private stored representation.
Recheck public configuration-key compatibility before changing the contract. (Converting Core Field Types, Creating Field Types)

do_not_assume: The version-scoped route remains correct for every Rock version.
Universal rendering removes the need for server authorization.
A working picker proves stored-value compatibility.
goal: A plugin field type whose C# implementation supplies structured picker data without owning UI code.
steps: Select the item, tree, or search picker pattern.
Define single- or multi-selection behavior.
Return the structured items or selected-item representations required by the pattern.
For tree or search data, implement the version-appropriate plugin API endpoint.
Under the supplied Rock 2.0 guidance, accept POST input from the request body and use an `api/v2/plugins/{organization-code}/...` route.
Apply ordinary authorization and any required grant evaluation in the endpoint.
Verify display, editing, stored-value conversion, and Data View filtering. (Universal Field Types)
